title.t: One message would start two playbooks

when.t: A message matches the start of two or more playbooks.

steps.t: The dispatcher delivers it to no one and asks the authorized user, naming each playbook: continue with the chosen one starts it; cancel drops the message.
No way in today: since the owner's comparables decision of 2026-10-21, no message starts two playbooks. The hold is tested with a made-up table where two playbooks share a start.

never.t: Pick a playbook on its own.

title.t: A playbook step would cross the closed track

when.t: During a playbook run, an agent sends something its track does not allow.

steps.t: The dispatcher refuses the message.
The run is halted and an integrity violation records it as a defect in the playbook, to be fixed in the playbook, not decided on the spot.

never.t: Let a playbook step override the track.

you_see.t: The halted playbook and the integrity record naming the defect.

test.t: During an open house run, the test, standing in as Agent 06, sends a client an invitation directly; only Agent 11 may message clients.

title.t: There is more work than capacity

when.t: While 25 or more questions wait for the authorized user, a message from outside the agents would start a new playbook run.

steps.t: The start waits; the authorized user is told once that the queue is full. Nothing is dropped.
When fewer than 25 questions wait, the waiting starts go in priority class order (1 escalation, 2 time-critical, 3 scheduled, 4 background, set per playbook), older first within a class.
The classes are per playbook; the tuple's five levels (escalations, transaction deadlines, client requests, internal work, discovery) are not separate classes in the code.

never.t: Let low-priority work jump the line.

you_see.t: One note that the queue is full; the record of the release order.

test.t: The test fills the queue with 25 questions (rejected settings), then a withdrawal, two new listings and a prospect arrive and wait. Three questions are marked done; the withdrawal goes first, then the two listings (older first), then the prospect.

title.t: A signed decision overrides a playbook step

when.t: A playbook holds a step for the authorized user, who signs a decision not to go ahead.

steps.t: The decision stands: the step does not happen.
The run ends and its after-action report lists the authorized user's signed decision.

never.t: Carry on against the signed decision.

you_see.t: The after-action report listing the decision.

test.t: The weekly seller report run (P18) holds this week's report; the authorized user cancels it. Nothing goes to the seller.

when.t: A comparables request includes a sale retrieved more than 30 days before.

steps.t: Agent 10 builds the package fresh, leaving out and counting the stale sale (10-04).

you_see.t: The package with one sale left out as stale.

test.t: A comparables request where one sale was retrieved too long ago.

title.t: One step fails while others go on

when.t: Filing a record in the client's drawer fails while the lead is being captured.

steps.t: The failure is recorded and held for the authorized user.
Capture, scoring and the record entries still complete.

never.t: Drop the job, or hide the failure.

you_see.t: A question about the failed filing; the rest done.

test.t: A lead under the thread name "Jane Synth": a name with a space cannot be a drawer folder.

when.t: A message with an ID the dispatcher has already seen arrives.

steps.t: The dispatcher answers it as a duplicate and does nothing else with it.

never.t: Act on the same message twice.

test.t: A test harness sends one inquiry twice with the same message ID.

title.t: It is unclear whether a legal line is crossed

when.t: An agent cannot verify something its legal line depends on.

steps.t: It treats it as crossed: in the test, Agent 08 cannot verify the sender of a settlement statement (no sender list), so it does not file it and raises a legal-line alert.
The statement is not filed, so the closing milestone is not met.

never.t: Give the benefit of the doubt on a legal question.

test.t: Closing October 20; a settlement statement arrives with no expected-sender list set.

when.t: An agent meets a case none of its tuples covers.

steps.t: It stops and asks the authorized user, saying no rule covers it.

you_see.t: A question saying no rule covers it.

test.t: A social mention "lol" labelled noise, which no Agent 20 rule covers.

title.t: Keeping the agents on their rules over long runs

when.t: A major step (a phase gate) is crossed, or an agent handles 10 messages with no gate.

steps.t: A re-reading of MANNERS.md is recorded on the audit log at each gate and at the 10-message backstop.
The agents are fixed code with nothing to re-read; the record is all that happens. Only Agent 04's model drafting prompt carries the MANNERS.md text, on every call.

never.t: Run long stretches without the record.

you_see.t: Nothing; the record shows each re-reading.

test.t: A new listing goes live; the record shows re-readings at its phase gates.

when.t: A message would go outside the system to a vendor, another party or the public.

steps.t: The dispatcher holds it until the authorized user signs its release.
Messages between the agents, and to the authorized user, go on.

never.t: Take an irreversible or public step without signed authority.

you_see.t: The photographer booking and the listing ad waiting for release.

test.t: A new listing: the photographer booking and the ad are both held for release.

title.t: Two jobs need the same agent at once

when.t: Waiting playbook starts are released and two of them go to the same agent.

steps.t: The higher class goes first; the other waits on a siding and resumes when the first is through. Neither is cancelled.
This applies only to work released from waiting; agents answer at once, so nothing waits mid-delivery.

never.t: Abort a job because of a clash.

you_see.t: Nothing; the record shows the hold and the resume.

test.t: With the queue full, a withdrawal and two new listings for Agent 05 and a prospect wait. On release the withdrawal goes first; the two listings wait on the siding and resume in arrival order; the prospect starts last.

title.t: A task would need a route that does not exist

when.t: A message is sent on a path the track does not declare.

steps.t: If the track knows the kind of message, the dispatcher refuses it before delivery.
If the kind of message is on no track at all, it is held and the authorized user is asked.

never.t: Treat a missing route as permission.

test.t: Standing in as Agent 06, the test asks Agent 14 for a client's record; that route does not exist.

title.t: No rule covers a situation during a playbook

when.t: During a playbook run, an agent asks the authorized user because no tuple covers a case.

steps.t: The agent holds it and asks.
The run's after-action report lists it as a proposed tuple, with the response left blank for the authorized user to ratify.

you_see.t: A question; a proposed tuple in the after-action report.

test.t: During an open house, a client asks "Can you run the ad on Instagram too?"; Agent 12 has no rule for it.
